section_summary: This section traces American efforts to remit funds from Japan and Dairen as Japanese exchange controls tightened in 1941. It includes individual company and citizen cases, proposals for controlling Japanese assets in the United States, and detailed Embassy reports on Japan’s July 1941 restrictions on foreign nationals’ property and transactions.

people.name: F. M. Prince
people.role: Vice President in Charge of Exports, The Paraffine Companies

people.name: Maxwell M. Hamilton
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Raymond C. Mackay
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Frank Woodey
people.role: American citizen seeking to remit funds from Dairen

people.name: Benninghoff
people.role: Second Secretary, American Embassy in Tokyo

people.name: Taro Terasaki
people.role: Director of the American Bureau, Japanese Foreign Office

subfiles.title: Proposed approach to Japan on treatment of American funds
subfiles.about: Grew proposes seeking assurances that American funds receive treatment as favorable as third-country funds.
subfiles.summary: Grew modifies his recommendation in a related telegram after a new Japanese ordinance.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese industrial and exchange controls
subfiles.about: The note points to Grew’s telegram on the effect of Japanese control laws on corporations.
subfiles.summary: References telegram 383, filed at 894.5034/23.

subfiles.title: Paraffine Companies request help remitting proceeds from Japan
subfiles.from: The Paraffine Companies, Inc., Export Division
subfiles.about: The company asks whether sale proceeds from its Japanese holdings could be converted and transferred to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The company reports Prince’s inquiry from Tokyo and its discussion with the Department. It requests further consideration of the difficulty of obtaining dollar exchange.

subfiles.title: Reply to the Paraffine Companies on remittance prospects
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains the limited prospects for predicting or securing a permit to remit liquidation proceeds.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the company’s representative in Japan can best assess the situation and the Embassy will give appropriate assistance. Capital remittances are often harder to obtain than remittances of dividends and profits.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Paraffine Companies correspondence
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the Prince conversation, the company’s letter, and its reply.
subfiles.summary: Transmits three papers concerning possible remittance of American funds from Japan.

subfiles.title: British funds and proposed Japanese exchange controls
subfiles.about: Sokobin reports British concern that new Japanese exchange controls may freeze British funds.
subfiles.summary: Press reports link British inquiries about deposits to proposed exchange controls. Sokobin has no independent confirmation but believes British authorities are concerned about a complete freeze.

subfiles.title: Representations concerning Frank Woodey’s exchange difficulties
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports its appeal to Japan’s Foreign Office concerning Woodey’s funds in Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses Chase’s letter, Chase’s appeal to the governor, and the Embassy’s oral statement. Terasaki promises to examine Woodey’s case but does not address the broader remittance question.

subfiles.title: Chase’s report on Woodey’s partial exchange permit
subfiles.from: A. S. Chase, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.about: Chase reports that Woodey received a permit for only part of the funds he sought to take to America.
subfiles.summary: After months of delay, Woodey receives permission to convert ¥4,000 of a revised ¥10,000 request. Chase seeks help for the remaining ¥6,000 and questions the authorities’ explanation that foreign exchange is unavailable.

subfiles.title: Appeal to Governor Yanai for Woodey’s remaining funds
subfiles.from: A. S. Chase, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.to: Yoshio Yanai, Governor of Kwantung Province
subfiles.about: Chase asks the governor to help Woodey convert and take out his remaining ¥6,000.
subfiles.summary: Chase describes Woodey’s planned permanent return to the United States and the prolonged delay on his exchange application. He argues that the partial permit and indefinite installment plan cause hardship and asks the governor to secure prompt release of the balance.

subfiles.title: Embassy oral statement on Woodey’s case
subfiles.about: The Embassy protests the delayed and partial release of Woodey’s funds.
subfiles.summary: The statement recounts Woodey’s unsuccessful applications and argues that Americans returning home should be able to transfer their assets. It invokes the freedom Japanese citizens have to remit funds from the United States.

subfiles.title: Gerli’s conversation with Wakasugi on Silk Guild remittances
subfiles.about: Gerli reports Wakasugi’s explanation for the halt in remittances collected in Japan for the International Silk Guild.
subfiles.summary: Wakasugi advises Gerli not to press for payment while relations between Japan and the United States remain uncertain. He expresses hope that the situation may become clearer by late May.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Gerli’s report
subfiles.about: The Department thanks Gerli for reporting his conversation about International Silk Guild funds.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Gerli’s letter and thanks him for keeping the Department informed.

subfiles.title: Savage’s transmittal of asset-control proposals
subfiles.about: Savage forwards a draft executive order and a memorandum of alternative exchange-control plans.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two papers at Dr. Feis’s request.

subfiles.title: Draft executive order on Japanese exchange and property
subfiles.about: The draft would establish a Cabinet committee and regulate Japanese exchange transactions and property in the United States.
subfiles.summary: The proposed order assigns policy to a committee of the Secretaries of State and Treasury and the Attorney General, with Treasury administering it. It prohibits specified transactions involving Japanese interests without authorization, requires reporting of Japanese-owned property, and provides for records, investigations, licensing, and penalties.

subfiles.title: Alternatives for exchange control and freezing
subfiles.about: The memorandum compares six approaches to foreign exchange control, property registration, and freezing Japanese accounts.
subfiles.summary: Options range from a comprehensive new executive order to targeted changes in Treasury licensing rules. Several would register foreign-owned property and give a Cabinet committee discretion over controls on Japanese accounts.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Prince about American funds in Japan
subfiles.about: Prince asks whether prospects have improved for remitting proceeds from a possible sale of company property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mackay says he knows of no recent improvement and cannot predict whether Japan will grant a permit. He suggests that the company’s representative in Japan consult the Embassy and local officials.

subfiles.title: New Japanese forward-exchange and concentration rules
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports new Japanese forward-exchange contracts and wider currency concentration rules.
subfiles.summary: Japan will require prompt bank settlement of trade exchange contracts and extend its concentration system to additional currencies.

subfiles.title: Japanese demands for American asset reports
subfiles.about: Japanese officials demand reports from American firms and individuals on their finances and property.
subfiles.summary: Grew interprets the reporting demands as preparation for freezing American credits in Japan.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram on American asset reports
subfiles.about: The memorandum restates Grew’s report on Japanese demands for American financial disclosures.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases telegram 1096 on possible freezing of American credits.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of telegram on Japan’s foreigner-transaction ordinance
subfiles.about: The Department sends Treasury copies of the Embassy’s report on Japan’s new ordinance.
subfiles.summary: Encloses five copies of telegram 1108.

subfiles.title: Summary of Japan’s foreigner-transaction ordinance
subfiles.about: Grew summarizes a 31-article Japanese ordinance restricting designated foreigners’ property and financial transactions.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance requires permits for many acquisitions, disposals, debts, loans, deposits, and currency transactions. It limits designated foreigners’ Japanese currency dealings to ¥500 monthly and requires initial and monthly reports of property, debts, and credits. A full translation is to follow.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of comparison of American and Japanese spending limits
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the Embassy’s comparison of Japanese and American limits on frozen nationals’ spending.
subfiles.summary: Encloses six copies of telegram 1111.

subfiles.title: Comparison of frozen nationals’ monthly allowances
subfiles.about: Grew compares the American $500 monthly allowance with Japan’s ¥500 limit.
subfiles.summary: Calls attention to the differing monthly limits in the two freezing orders.

subfiles.title: Request for instructions on transmitting ordinance translation
subfiles.about: The Embassy asks whether its 14-page translation should go by pouch or naval radio.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission instructions for telegram 1142.

subfiles.title: General licenses under Japan’s new ordinance
subfiles.about: Japan creates limited general-license exemptions from its controls on foreigners’ transactions.
subfiles.summary: Exemptions cover certain taxes, Japanese employee salaries, government charges, and import payments.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of telegram on general licenses
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the Embassy’s report on Japan’s transaction-control exemptions.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of telegram 1156.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on withdrawals from frozen Yokohama Specie Bank accounts
subfiles.about: The note points to a Chefoo telegram on American and British firms’ frozen accounts and local exchange licensing.
subfiles.summary: References Roberts’s telegram 15, filed at 893.115/1142.

subfiles.title: Shanghai awaits transmission instructions
subfiles.about: Shanghai reports holding the ordinance translation while awaiting instructions.
subfiles.summary: Requests an expedited decision on transmitting Tokyo’s message.

subfiles.title: Instruction to send the ordinance translation
subfiles.about: The Department instructs Shanghai to forward Tokyo’s ordinance translation.
subfiles.summary: Directs transmission of the material by naval radio.

subfiles.title: Translation of Japan’s regulations controlling transactions involving foreigners
subfiles.about: The Embassy transmits a translation of the Japanese Finance Ministry ordinance restricting transactions involving designated foreign nationals.
subfiles.summary: The translation defines designated nations, nationals, residents, and connected businesses. It sets permit requirements for property, currency, debts, investments, leases, loans, deposits, and third-party dealings, while allowing specified exemptions. It also requires initial and monthly reports of holdings, claims, debts, investments, and acts performed for designated foreign nationals. The translation continues beyond page 240.
